summary: Learn Terraform modules, state, providers, and plan review in 5 days. Build practical IaC workflows for reliable cloud delivery.
lede: Infrastructure as Code with Terraform helps you define cloud infrastructure in versioned configuration, then provision, update, and track resources consistently across environments. This course develops practical skills in HCL, provider configuration, reusable modules, variables, outputs, state management, remote backends, and plan and apply workflows. You will practise reviewing execution plans, controlling infrastructure changes through Git-based workflows, and setting up remote state for more disciplined delivery. The course also introduces policy as code, drift detection, and CI/CD automation so you can reduce manual intervention, improve reproducibility, and support clearer rollback and change-control practices.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who already work around cloud environments and need to make Infrastructure as Code with Terraform reliable, reusable, and governable.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of cloud infrastructure concepts, basic Linux or Windows administration, and familiarity with Git and command-line workflows. Basic exposure to one major cloud platform is helpful, but prior Terraform experience is not required. Coding/programming is not required for completion, although you should be comfortable editing configuration files and reading command output. Advanced concepts such as remote state, modules, and policy-aware workflows are taught at an operational level with hands-on practice.
